harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed a root crontab entry on node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15, appending stdout/stderr to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified functionally, then performed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, crond active, crontab, log contents), issued a native reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and confirmed post-restart recovery of crond (active+enabled), the crontab entry, and the log file/contents.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: confirmed /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script exists and is executable, crond is active, no prior root crontab, no prior log file, sudo available non-interactively.
Installed root crontab entry: '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' via `sudo crontab -u root -`.
Manually ran the exact cron command line to verify it creates/appends to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log correctly.
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, crond active state, crontab contents, log file contents.
Issued `sudo shutdown -r now` backgrounded with nohup so the ack returned before disconnect.
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again (two timeouts, then success).
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, proving an actual reboot occurred.
Verified post-restart recovery: crond active and enabled, root crontab entry intact, log file and its content preserved, maintenance script still present and executable.

evidence.requirement: Cron job configured: /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance runs daily at 02:15, output retained in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Confirmed pre-state (no crontab/log), installed root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', then manually executed the exact command and confirmed the log file was created with the script's output appended.
Captured boot_id (738d0aac-71a1-4191-8a37-bf00edfeff5d), crond active, crontab entry present, and log file contents prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `sudo shutdown -r now`; command returned 'reboot-issued' successfully before the node went offline.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable for two poll attempts (connection timed out during reboot), then reconnected with a new boot_id (2ab54a3e-3cb7-45ee-b2b3-a7d1edde834b), differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real kernel restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After reconnecting, confirmed crond is active and enabled, the root crontab entry for inventory-maintenance is intact, /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log and its prior content survived the restart, and the maintenance script is still present and executable.
